blocks.orig: For many, climbing Mount Kilimanjaro is the – wait for it – peak of their hiking aspirations. At a breathtaking 5,895 metres above sea level, Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa and the highest freestanding mountain in the world. So, it goes without saying that the process of summiting this mighty mountain comes with a healthy dose of challenges. At Your Tanzania Trip, one of the main questions our Kilimanjaro clients ask us is how you prepare for this bucket-list adventure in Africa?
blocks.html: For plenty of hikers, Mount Kilimanjaro is the – wait for it – peak of their ambitions. Rising to a breathtaking 5,895 metres above sea level, it is the tallest peak on the African continent and the loftiest freestanding mountain on the planet. It follows, then, that getting to the top of this giant brings its fair share of difficulties. Among the things our Kilimanjaro clients ask Your Tanzania Trip most often is: how do you get ready for this bucket-list adventure in Africa?

blocks.orig: Paul and Nico, our experienced Your Tanzania Trip mountain climbing guides, have safely and successfully guided numerous climbers to the top of the Kilimanjaro of varying experience levels. Here, they share their top five tips for success on your trek to Mount Kilimanjaro.
blocks.html: Our seasoned Your Tanzania Trip mountain guides Paul and Nico have led a great many climbers, from beginners to veterans, safely and successfully to the summit of Kilimanjaro. Below they pass on their five best tips for a successful trek up Mount Kilimanjaro.

blocks.orig: Since climbing the Kilimanjaro is not a marathon, you don’t have to run for several hours to reach the summit. Before you arrive in Tanzania, ensure your body is already accustomed to walking long distances. Practice hikes that last multiple hours and even days. Take it at a slow, steady speed with some breaks in between. Your feet will thank you for it!
blocks.html: Climbing Kilimanjaro is no marathon: there is no need to run for hours on end to reach the top. What you should do is make sure your body is used to walking long distances before you land in Tanzania. Go on practice hikes of several hours, or even several days, at a slow, steady pace with breaks along the way. Your feet will be grateful!

blocks.orig: Good health, a positive attitude, and stamina are the most critical prerequisites to reaching Mt Kilimanjaro’s top. Stamina is much more important than strength and is quickly built up by hiking in areas closer to home. Use the months leading up to your Tanzania climbing trip to see what hike level you are comfortable with. Slowly increase the duration and intensity of your hikes until you are pleased with how you feel on treks lasting two days or more.
blocks.html: Being in good health, keeping a positive mindset and having stamina are the essentials for reaching the top of Mt Kilimanjaro. Stamina counts for far more than strength, and you can build it quickly by hiking closer to home. In the months before your Tanzania climbing trip, find out what level of hike feels comfortable, then gradually extend the length and intensity of your walks until you feel good on treks of two days or longer.

blocks.orig: For top-notch preparation for your Mount Kilimanjaro trek, you should know what’s coming. During your ascent, you will come across a beautiful variety of landscapes with sometimes drastically different temperatures. The right clothes and the ideal equipment are therefore essential. Check out our short packing list with some must-haves to get an idea. After booking with Your Tanzania Trip, you will, of course, receive a list with everything you will need.
blocks.html: To prepare properly for your Mount Kilimanjaro trek, it helps to know what lies ahead. On the way up you pass through a striking range of landscapes, where the temperature can swing dramatically. Suitable clothing and the right equipment are therefore vital. Our short packing list of must-haves below gives you a first impression; once you have booked with Your Tanzania Trip, you will naturally receive a complete list of everything you need.

blocks.orig: Ankle-high hiking boots, already broken in!
blocks.html: Hiking boots that cover the ankle, worn in beforehand!

blocks.orig: Sleeping bag up to -2 °C or down sleeping bag
blocks.html: A sleeping bag rated to -2 °C, or a down sleeping bag

blocks.orig: Energy bars – you will get three meals a day; a snack never hurts, though 😉
blocks.html: Energy bars – three meals a day are provided, but an extra snack never goes amiss 😉

blocks.orig: Water bottle or bladder – you should drink around three to four litres of water a day on your Mt Kilimanjaro trek, and you can fill up your water during your hike.
blocks.html: A bottle or hydration bladder – aim for roughly three to four litres of fluid daily while trekking Mt Kilimanjaro; topping up along the route is possible.

blocks.orig: Another excellent tip for preparing for Mount Kilimanjaro is to wear your backpack and the same hiking gear during your training at home. This enables you to get used to the weight and find out what you need to wear without getting too cold or hot. This will also allow you to figure out what requires adjusting in your equipment and if you are missing any necessary accessories.
blocks.html: Another very useful way of preparing for Mount Kilimanjaro is to train at home wearing your backpack and the same hiking gear you will take with you. That way you get accustomed to the weight and learn what to wear so you are neither too cold nor too warm. You will also discover what needs adjusting in your kit and whether any essential accessories are still missing.

blocks.orig: Since nobody knows what the weather will be like during your tour, try to train in all weathers – rainy days included! In doing so, you can get adjusted to different conditions and strengthen your immune system, increasing your chances to reach the summit. That’s the goal, after all!
blocks.html: Nobody can predict the weather you will get on your tour, so try to train in every kind of weather – wet days included! This helps you adapt to varying conditions and toughens your immune system, which improves your odds of making the summit. And that, after all, is what it is all about!

blocks.orig: This wisdom has some truth, since you can build energy through training and the proper diet. Treat your body and muscles (you will need them for your ascent!) with a lot of healthy food and eat regularly. Then you will progress faster and prevent aching muscles – nobody needs those, right?
blocks.html: There is some truth in that saying, because training and a proper diet build up your energy reserves. Look after your body and your muscles (you are going to need them on the way up!) by eating plenty of healthy food at regular times. You will make faster progress and avoid sore muscles – and who needs those?

blocks.orig: This is probably the most important tip: climbing Kilimanjaro requires expertise and professional guidance. Do your research when it comes to booking with a Tanzania travel company, and make sure you feel safe and comfortable before you book anything.
blocks.html: This may well be the most important tip of all: climbing Kilimanjaro calls for expertise and professional guidance. Do your homework before booking with a Tanzania travel company, and only commit once you feel safe and at ease.

blocks.orig: Even for the most experienced hikers, the benefits of tapping into the local knowledge of a Kilimanjaro mountain guide can make the difference between summiting or not. Not only do they know the best routes, but they also watch out for you during your hike: they notice signs of altitude sickness, measure your heart rate and level of oxygen and discuss all your results with you to keep you healthy.
blocks.html: Even for highly experienced hikers, drawing on the local knowledge of a Kilimanjaro mountain guide can decide whether you reach the summit or not. They know the best routes, but they also keep an eye on you throughout the hike: spotting signs of altitude sickness, checking your heart rate and oxygen level, and talking through all the readings with you to keep you healthy.
